sections.title: Power Rule Differentiation
sections.description: Partial derivatives of polynomial functions use the power rule while treating other variables as constants.

sections.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Rules
sections.description: Differentiation formulas for exponential and natural log functions apply to partial derivatives involving multiple variables.

sections.title: Chain Rule and Square Roots
sections.description: Calculating partial derivatives for square root functions requires applying the chain rule to the inner terms.

sections.title: Trigonometry and Numerical Evaluation
sections.description: Partial derivatives for trigonometric functions are found before substituting specific coordinates to find numerical values.

sections.title: Product Rule Selection
sections.description: The product rule is necessary only when the variable of differentiation appears in multiple factors.

sections.title: Quotient Rule Selection
sections.description: The quotient rule must be used when both the numerator and denominator contain the differentiation variable.

sections.title: Functions of Three Variables
sections.description: Partial differentiation extends to functions with three variables by treating two variables as constants simultaneously.

sections.title: Complex Multi-Variable Evaluation
sections.description: Advanced examples demonstrate combining product rules with three-variable functions to find rates of change.

sections.title: Higher Order Derivatives
sections.description: Finding second and third order partial derivatives involves repeatedly differentiating the function with respect to specific variables.

sections.title: Equality of Mixed Partials
sections.description: Mixed partial derivatives are equal regardless of differentiation order if the function remains continuous.
